passage.title: The Lost Lunchbox
passage.text:
Maya packed her own lunch every morning. Today it held a cheese sandwich, a mandarin, and four crackers. She placed the lunchbox on the classroom shelf next to eleven identical red boxes — the same brand as everyone else in her class.

At lunchtime, Maya's box was missing from its usual spot. She checked under the table and inside her bag before asking her teacher, Mrs Lee, for help.

Sam handed her a lunchbox that looked identical to hers. Maya opened it and found a banana and a cheese stick instead of her mandarin and crackers. “This isn’t my lunch,” she said, comparing the two boxes side by side.

Mrs Lee discovered Maya’s real lunchbox behind the door, where it had been knocked off the shelf. Maya and Sam agreed to write their names on their boxes from then on, so this would never happen again.

glossary.meaning: A flat board on a wall where you put things.

sentences.text: The bus stopped at the shop.
Sam handed her a red lunchbox.
They wrote their names on their boxes.
Mrs Lee found the lunchbox behind the door.
Labelling your things helps you tell them apart.

listen.prompt: Where did Sam put his hat?
listen.hint: Listen for where the hat went.
listen.say: Sam hung his hat on the hook by the classroom door.

listen.prompt: What did Maya buy at the shop?
listen.hint: Listen for the two things she bought.
listen.say: At the corner shop, Maya bought milk and eggs for breakfast.

listen.prompt: Why did everyone stop at the crossing?
listen.say: Everyone stopped at the crossing because the light was red.

listen.prompt: Where did the class go after the library?
listen.hint: Listen for the order of places.
listen.say: First the class visited the library, then the museum, and last they had lunch in the park.

listen.prompt: How many children were on the bus at the end?
listen.hint: Start with six, then add three.

mission.title: The Great Lunchbox Mix-Up
mission.goal: Find the town's lost name labels and the Compass piece!

intro.line: Hello, Sparky! I'm Mrs Hoot, the town librarian. Busy Town has had a big mix-up!
Everybody's lunchboxes look the same, and all the name labels blew away in the wind.
Let's find the labels and sort it out, Mrs Hoot!
First, read Maya's story on the Story Stone. It's all about a lunchbox mix-up.

beats.setup: Tweet! I'm Pip, I deliver the mail. Listen to my message, and I'll show you where the labels flew!
beats.success: Tweet! That's right! This way, past the bus stop!
beats.fail: Tweet? That's not what I said. Listen again!
beats.clue: Pip saw the labels fly past the bus stop

beats.setup: The street sign got knocked round in the wind. Answer a question about Maya's story to fix it.
beats.success: The sign points to the park now!
beats.fail: Oh dear, still spinning. Let's read the story again.
beats.clue: The street sign points to the park

beats.setup: Ahem. I'm Old Stony, the park statue. Tell me what these story words mean and I'll open the park gate.
beats.success: Very good. The gate is open.
beats.fail: Ahem, not quite. The gate stays closed.
beats.clue: Old Stony opened the park gate

beats.setup: G'day! The bridge over the creek is missing planks. Count them with me and we'll fix it!
beats.success: Bonzer! The bridge is fixed. Across you go!
beats.fail: Oops, the planks fell in the creek. Let's count again.

beats.setup: The ivy on the library wall wilted. Use your science brain to bring it back so you can climb!
beats.success: Wonderful! The ivy is green and strong!
beats.fail: Hmm, it's still wilted. Think again.
beats.clue: The library ivy is green again

beats.setup: My bakery box has a pattern lock. Work out what comes next to open it.
beats.success: Click! The labels are inside, and a clue: X marks the spot in the town square!
beats.fail: Clunk. Still locked. Look at the pattern again.
beats.clue: X marks the spot in the town square

beats.setup: The town hall door needs a password. Listen carefully and write it!
beats.success: The town hall is open! The town square is just ahead!
beats.fail: That's not the password. Let's try again.

finale.line: Everyone has their name labels back! And look, an X in the town square. Dig, Sparky, dig!
Another piece of the Heartwood Compass!
Bonzer! Take it back to Wildlands, mate. The Heartwood will love it.
